Hadhrat Sa'd Qaradh (RA) immediately climbed up a date palm and called out the Adhaan. "What made you call out the Adhaan, O Sa'd?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) replied, "May my parents be sacrificed for you! I saw you with only a handful of people and did not see Bilaal with you. When I then noticed the slaves looking at each other and then at you, I feared that they would harm you, so I called out the Adhaan (so that other Muslims would come quickly)." "You did the right thing, O Sa'd," Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Whenever you see Bilaal not with me, you should call out the Adhaan." Thereafter, Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) called out the Adhaan thrice during Rasulullaah ﷺ's lifetime.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.336) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) said, "The share (of rewards) of those who call out the Adhaan on the Day of Qiyaamah will be like the share of those who wage Jihaad. During the time between the Adhaan and the Iqaamah, the Mu'adhin is like the martyr tossing and turning in his blood in the path of Allaah. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "If I were a Mu'adhin, I care not whether I perform Hajj or Umrah or wage Jihaad."

Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) said, "If I were a Mu'adhin, my affairs would have been perfected and I care not whether I woke up for (Nafl) salaah during the night or whether I fasted (Nafl fasts) during the day because I heard Rasulullaah pray, 'O Allaah! Forgive those who call out the Adhaan. O Allaah! Forgive those who call out the Adhaan.' 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I said, 'But (why do you emphasise calling out the Adhaan so much when) you have left us in a condition that we would draw swords to call out the Adhaan?' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'That is not the case, O Umar because there will soon come a time when people will leave the Adhaan to the weak ones amongst them. The flesh that is forbidden for Jahannam is the flesh of those who call out the Adhaan.'" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) mentioned that it is the Mu'adhin to whom Allaah refers in the verse: yi tf Jbj Vy Whose speech can be better than the one who calls (others) towards Allaah, who performs righteous deeds, and (humbly) says, "1 am from the Muslims (from those who submit to Allaah)." (Surah Sajdah, verse 33)
She says further, "The Mu'adhin calls towards Allaah when he says 'jji Js- '
('Come to salaah'), he performs a righteous deed when he performs the salaah and he is certainly amongst the Muslims when he says, Vj y ' ('There is none worthy of worship but Allaah')."
sources: Bayhaqi in his Shu'abul Imaan, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.265). Abush Sheikh has reported simrlar narrations from Rasaafi in his Kitaabul Adhaan, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.266).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "Had I been a Mu'adhin, I care not if I neither perform Hajj or Umrah except for the Fardh Hajj. Had the angels descended on earth, none would be able to beat them to calling out the Adhaan (they would allow no one else to do it because they know its tremendous virtue)."
sources: Ibnuz Zanjway, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.265).

paras: Hadhrat Qais bin Abu Haazim narrates that when they went to Hadhrat Umar he asked, "Who calls out the Adhaan amongst you people?" When they informed him that it was their slaves who did it, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "That is a grave deficiency in you. Had I the choice of being a Mu'adhin instead of the Khalifah, I would have chosen to be a Mu'adhin.
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.265).

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I regret not requesting Rasulullaah ﷺ to assign the duty of calling out the Adhaan to (my sons) Hasan and Husayn."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.326) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "I do not approve of you appointing blind people to call out the Adhaan (because they are unable to determine the correct times of salaah) and I also do not approve of you appointing learned scholars of the Qur'aan to call out the Adhaan (because this would affect their teaching)."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.2).

paras: Hadhrat Yahya Bakkaa narrates that a man once said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar, "I love you for the sake of Allaah." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar responded by saying, "But I detest you for the sake of Allaah." When the man asked why this was, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) replied, "Because you adopt a singing tone when calling out the Adhaan and you take payment for it."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.3) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: When Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed bin Al Aas to Yemen, he gave him instructions to take as prisoners the inhabitants of all the towns he passed in which the Adhaan was not called out. Therefore, when Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) passed by the Banu Zubayd tribe and did not hear them call out the Adhaan, he took them all as prisoners. However, when Hadhrat Amr bin Ma'dikarib spoke to him about them, Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) eleased them into his custody. Hadhrat Talha bin Abdullaah bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) dispatched his armies against the Murtaddeen, he instructed the commanders saying, "When you hear the Adhaan in a town that you surround, take no action until you question them about their grievances. However, if you do not hear the Adhaan, you should launch your attack, fight them, burn their property and be inexhaustible in inflicting casualties so that they see that the demise of your Nabi ﷺ has brought no weakness in you."
sources: Bayhaqi.

paras: Hadhrat Zuhri narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr 5S5.l2ffiSg dispatched his armies against the Murtaddeen, he instructed them saying, "Monitor them overnight and take no action if you hear the Adhaan because the Adhaan is a sign of Imaan."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg. 141).

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that when the time for salaah arrived and Rasulullaah ﷺ saw that the people were few in number, he remain sitting and did not lead the salaah. He would then lead the salaah only when he saw a substantial gathering.
sources: Abu Dawood, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.246).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Awfa (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ would wait until he heard the sounds of people's shoes.
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.247).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy dispatching an army until half the night had already passed or was about to. He then came out for salaah and said (to those waiting), "While other people have performed their salaah and left, you people are still waiting for salaah. Take note that you have remained in salaah (kept earning its rewards) as long as you have been waiting for it."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg. 193). (6) Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.245). Ibn Maajah has also reported the narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), as Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 1 Pg.246).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that after Rasulullaah ﷺ had performed the Maghrib salaah, some people left while others remained seated. Rasulullaah ﷺ then went to them (those still sitting) and said, "Your Rabb has opened a door to the heavens and is boasting before the angels saying, 'My servants have completed a Fardh and are now waiting for the next.'"'

Hadhrat Abu Umaamah Thaqafi (RA) reports that after leading the Zuhr salaah, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) told the people to remain where they were until he returned. He then left and put on his shawl. After leading the Asr salaah, he said, "Should 1 not inform you of something that Rasulullaah ﷺ did?" When the people asked to be informed, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) said, "The Sahabah once performed the Zuhr salaah behind Rasulullaah ﷺ and then remained sitting. When Rasulullaah ﷺ came out again (for the Asr salaah), he asked, 'Have you people not left after the last salaah?' 'No,' came the reply. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, 'If only you could have seen your Rabb open a door from the heavens to show you to the angels and boast about you sitting in wait for salaah.
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id ' (Vol.2 Pg.38).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delayed the Isha salaah until midnight. After leading the salaah, he turned to face the Sahabah saying, "Whereas other people have already performed their salaah and gone to sleep, you people have remained in salaah for as long as you have been waiting for it."
sources: Bukhaari.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Rasool ﷺ said, "A person is in salaah for as long as it is salaah that keeps him waiting and (all the while) the angels keep praying, 'O Allaah! Forgive him. O Allaah! Shower Your mercy on him.' This continues for as long as he does not stand up from his place of salaah or does not break his wudhu."
sources: Bukhaari.

paras: Another narration states that a person remains in salaah for as long as he remains on his place of salaah or as long as he does not break his wudhu." ^ Yet another narration states that a person remains in salaah for as long as he remains on his place of salaah, waiting for the next salaah. And all this while the angels keep praying, 'O Allaah! Forgive him. O Allaah! Shower Your mercy on him.' This continues for as long as he does not leave or does not break his wudhu." "How will his wudhu break?" one of the narrators asked. Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah replied, "When he passes wind either audibly or silently."
sources: Muslim and Abu Dawood.

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Shall I not point you towards something that wipes out sins and is expiation for misdeeds?" "Why not, O Rasulullaah ﷺ the Sahabah (RA) said. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Making a proper wudhu in adverse conditions, taking many steps towards the Masjid and waiting for one salaah after another. This is (an act that will earn the reward of) guarding the borders."
sources: Ibn Hibbaan, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.247).

paras: Hadhrat Dawood bin Saalih narrates that Hadhrat Abu Salamah once asked him if he knew why Allaah revealed the verse-.

Exercise patience, compete in patience, guard the borders... (Surah Aal Imraan, verse 200) When Hadhrat Dawood admitted that he did not know, Hadhrat Abu Salamah said, "I heard Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) say that during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ there was no war because of which the borders had to be guarded, but waiting for one salaah after another was their form of guarding the borders."
sources: Haakim, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 1 Pg.251).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) said that it is waiting for the Isha salaah that is referred to in the verse: ij s-yycr Their sides part from their beds... (Surah Sajdah, verse 16)
sources: Tirmidhi, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.246).

paras: Hadhrat Amr bin Ummu Maktoom (RA) once said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I am a blind man who lives far (from the Masjid). While I have a guide, he is a person with whom I cannot get along. Are you able to grant me permission to perform salaah at home?" "Can you hear the Adhaan?" Rasulullaah ijfil asked. When Hadhrat Amr (RA) said that he could, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I am then unable to grant you permission."

Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came to the Masjid and found only a few people there. He then said, "I have a good mind to appoint an Imaam to lead the people (in salaah) and to then go out and burn down the house of every person I find who does not come for salaah." Hadhrat Ibn Ummu Maktoom then said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ There are many palms and trees between my house and the Masjid and I cannot find a guide at all times. Is it possible for me to perform salaah at home?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Can you hear the Iqaamah?" When he replied that he could, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Then you should come (to the Masjid) for salaah."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.235).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "Whoever wishes to meet Allaah tomorrow as a Muslim should regularly perform these (Fardh) salaahs in the place where the Adhaan is called out because Allaah has selected for His Nabi certain practices that give guidance and amongst these practices are the salaahs (in congregation). Should you ever perform your salaah at your homes as those staying behind at home do, you will be forsaking the Sunnah of your Nabi ﷺ and as soon as you do this, you will go astray. Whenever a person purifies himself properly and then heads for one of the Masaajid, Allaah records for him the reward of a good deed for every step he takes, Allaah elevates his rank by a stage and erases a sin from his record. I saw (a time when) none of us would dare miss a salaah (in congregation) except for an open hypocrite. In fact, a man (who was very ill) would be brought with the support of two men and placed in the row."

Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, " I saw (a time when) none of us would dare miss a salaah (in congregation) except for a person whom everyone recognised as a hypocrite or a very sick person. If a (sick) man was capable of walking with the support of two men, he would come for the salaah." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also added, "Verily our Nabi ﷺ has taught us certain practices that give guidance and amongst these practices is to perform salaah in the Masjid where Adhaan was called out."
sources: Tabraani and Ibn Khuzaymah, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.232). Sa'eed bin Mansoor has also reported the narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.244), as has Bazzaar, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.40).

paras: A narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) added, "And now 1 cannot find who does not have a place of salaah inside his house where he performs salaah. If you perform salaah in your homes and forsake the Masaajid, you will be forsaking the Sunnah of your Nabi ﷺ ,"
sources: Maalik, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 1 Pg.235).

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) said, "Whoever would like to go peacefully to Allaah should perform these five (Fardh) salaahs at a place where the Adhaan is called out because these are amongst the practices that give guidance and what your Nabi ﷺ practically showed you. You should never say that you have reserved a place in your house where you perform salaah because if you do that (1 ) Ahmad, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 1 Pg.238). you will be forsaking the Sunnah of your Nabi ﷺ and as soon as you forsake his Sunnah, you will go astray."
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "When we did not see a person for the Fajr and Isha salaahs, we became suspicious of him (because it is the Munaafiqeen who do not perform these salaahs)."

Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Sulaymaan bin Abu Hathma narrates that Hadhrat Umar once did not see Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Abu Hathma (RA) for the Fajr salaah. Hadhrat Umar (RA) was on his way to the marketplace that morning and because Hadhrat Sulaymaan (RA)'s house happened to be between the Masjid and the marketplace, Hadhrat Umar (RA) passed by Hadhrat Sulaymaan .'s mother Hadhrat Shifaa (RA). "I did not see Sulaymaan for the Fajr salaah," Hadhrat Umar (RA) said. She explained, "He spent the night in salaah and sleep overpowered him." To this, Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, "I prefer attending the Fajr salaah in congregation to standing in salaah all night." Hadhrat Ibn Abu Mulaykah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Shifaa (RA) who belonged to the bin Ka"b tribe once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) during Ramadhaan. Enquiring about her husband, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Why did I not see Abu Hathma for the Fajr salaah?" "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" she explained, "He exerted himself (in Ibaadah) throughout the night and was too tired to go out to perform the Fajr salaah, so he (performed salaah at home and) slept." Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, "By Allaah! Had he been present for the Fajr salaah, it would have been more beloved to me than his exertion throughout the night."

In another narration, Hadhrat Shifaa bint Abdullaah (RA) says, "Hadhrat Umar once came to my house where he found two men (my husband and son) fast asleep. 'What is the matter with these two that they were not present with us for salaah?' he asked. 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen!' I explained, They fell asleep after performing their Fajr salaah (at home).' To this Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, 'I prefer performing Fajr salaah in congregation to performing (Nafl) salaah throughout the night and until dawn."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.243).

paras: Hadhrat Ummu Dardaa (RA) says that when (her husband) Hadhrat Abu Dardaa once came home angry, she asked him what the matter was. He replied, "By Allaah! I know nothing else about the affairs of Muhammad ﷺ except that the Muslims performed salaah only in congregation (and now people are starting to do otherwise)."
Hadhrat Naafi narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) missed the Isha salaah in congregation, he would remain in Ibaadah for the rest of the night.
sources: Bukhaari.

paras: Another narration states that whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar missed any salaah in congregation, he would remain engaged in salaah until the next salaah.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg.303).

paras: Hadhrat Ambasah bin Azhar narrates that it was customary for a newly married man to remain indoors for a few days after getting married and not to leave for the Fajr salaah. However, when a Sahabi by the name of Hadhrat Haarith bin Hassaan was married, he was leaving for Fajr when someone taunted, "You are leaving when you have just married this night?" Hadhrat Haarith (RA) said, "By Allaah! The woman who prevents me from performing the Fajr salaah in congregation is a terrible woman indeed."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in lsaabah (Vol.2 Pg.349).

paras: Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to go to the ends of the rows and straighten the chests and shoulders of the people saying, "Do not be in disarray otherwise your hearts will be in disarray (will be disunited). Verily Allaah bestows His special mercy on the people standing in the first row and the angels pray for their forgiveness."
sources: Ibn Khuzaymah, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.282).

paras: Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to weave between the rows from one end to the other, touching our chests and shoulders (when straightening the rows) and saying, 'Do not stand in disarray.
sources: Abu Dawood, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 1 Pg.289).

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samurah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out to them and said, "Will you not form your rows as the angels form theirs in front of their Rabb?" When the Sahabah (RA) enquired how it was that the angels formed their rows, Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "They first complete the front rows and stand close to each other."
sources: Muslim, Abu Dawood, Nasa'ee and Ibn Maajah, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 1 Pg.283).

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samurah (RA) also narrates that they were once performing salaah with Rasulullaah ﷺ when he motioned them to sit down. When they sat down, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "What prevents you from forming your rows as the angels form theirs?" The rest of the narration is similar to the one above.
sources: Abu Dawood and ibn Maajah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.255).

paras: Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to straighten our rows as meticulously as he would straighten an arrow. This he did until we had understood him perfectly. On one occasion when Rasulullaah ﷺ came out for salaah, he stood there and was about to say 'Allaahu Akbar' when he noticed someone's chest standing out from the row. He then said, 'O servants of Allaah! You will have to straighten your rows otherwise Allaah will cast disunity between you."
sources: Maalik, Muslim, Abu Dawood, Tirmidhi, Ibn Maajah and Nasa'ee.

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Nu'maan (RA) added, "I then saw a man touching his shoulders with those of the person beside him, touching his knees with those of the other man and also touching his ankles with those of the other man."
sources: Abu Dawood, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.289).

paras: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to instruct the people to straighten their rows and it was only when they reported to him that the rows were straightened did he call out the Takbeer (to commence the salaah).
sources: Maalik, Abdur Razzaaq and Bayhaqi.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi (RA) reports that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to instruct the people to straighten their rows and would actually call people by their names to tell them to move forward. He also said, "When people keep staying back, Allaah will eventually keep them back."

Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan (RA) also reports that he noticed that whenever Hadhrat Umar (RA) stepped forward (to lead the salaah), he would look at the shoulders and feet of the followers (to see if they were in line)."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 4 Pg.254-255).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Nadhar narrates that when salaah was about to begin, Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab would tell people to straighten their rows and would take people's names as he told them to either move forward or backward. He would also add, "Keep your rows straight because Allaah wishes you to adopt the method of the angels (when they form their rows)." He would then recited the verse: "Indeed, we (the angels) axe standing in rows (worshipping Allaah").' Indeed, we are glorifying Allaah (all the time)." (Surah Saafaat, verses 165.166)
sources: Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jareer and Ibn Abi Haatim, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 4 Pg.255).

paras: Hadhrat Maalik says, "I was with Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) when the people stood up for salaah. I was busy requesting him to grant me an allowance and continued doing so as he straightened some pebbles with his shoe.
Eventually some men whom he had appointed to straighten the rows reported to him that the rows had been straightened. He then told me to stand straight in one of the rows and called out the Takbeer."

Another narration states that Hadhrat Ali (RA) used to say (to the people standing in rows for salaah), "Stand straight and your hearts will be straight, stand close to each other and you will have compassion for each other."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg,255).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "I saw a time when salaah would not begin until we had completed the rows of salaah."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "Verily Allaah bestows His special mercy on the people who advance through the rows to the first row of salaah and the angels pray for their forgiveness." Statements of Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas Concerning the First Row Hadhrat Abdul Azeez bin Rufay reports, "It was during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr that Hadhrat Aamir bin Mas'ood Qurashi (RA) was trying to get ahead of me to the first row at the Maqaam in Makkah. 'Is there much good mentioned about the first row?' I asked. 'By Allaah! There certainly is,' he replied, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said that if people realised the value of the first row, the only way in which the rows would be formed would be by drawing lots."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.255).
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.92) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Ensure that you always stand in the first row and ensure that it is on the right of the first row. You should also refrain from forming rows between pillars."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.92) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Qais bin Ubaadah says, "I was present in Madinah when the people stood up for salaah. I then forged ahead and stood in the first row. Hadhrat Umar arrived and made his way through the rows to get to the front (to lead the salaah). With him was a tanned man with a sparse beard. Looking the faces of the people there, his eyes fell on me and he pushed me aside stand in my place. This hurt me very deeply. However, when the salaah was ovei. he turned to me and said, 'Let not what had happened upset you or cause you grief because I am sure that it hurt you. However, I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that none save the Muhaajireen and Ansaar should occupy the first row.' When I asked the people who the man was, they informed me that he was Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b In another narration, Hadhrat Qais says, "As I was performing salaah in the first row of the Masjid of Madinah, someone came from behind, pulled me back and stood in my place. the salaah was over, he turned to me and I realised that he was Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA). He then said to me, "May Allaah never make you upset, dear youngster. This was something that Rasulullaah ﷺ enjoined upon us..." The narration then continues like the one above.
sources: Haakim in his Mustadrak (Vol.3 Pg.303), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.

paras: Hadhrat Usaamah bin Umayr (RA) says, "People would have already stood up for salaah when a person would stand between Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Qibla, presenting his need to Rasulullaah ﷺ. He would remain standing there and talking with Rasulullaah ﷺ for such a long time that I sometimes saw some people nodding off to sleep because of the long while Rasulullaah ﷺ had to remain standing there."

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that the people would be ready to perform the Isha salaah when Rasulullaah ﷺ needed to speak to a person. A few of the Sahabah would actually fall asleep (during the wait) and would then wake up when the salaah began. '''

Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that people would discuss their needs with Rasulullaah ﷺ after the Mu'adhin had called out the Iqaamah and the people had already hushed. Rasulullaah ﷺ would then see tpat the need was fulfilled. Hadhrat Anas (RA) mentions that Rasulullaah ﷺ had a staff on which he would lean (when the dialogue became too long).
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.273).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was the most compassionate of people and whenever someone came to him (with a request), he would promise it to him (if he did not have then) and then give it to him when he had it. People had already stood up for salaah one day when a Bedouin arrived and, grabbing on to Rasulullaah ﷺ's clothing, he demanded, 'A small portion of what I need is still due and I fear that I may forget about it (so I want it now).' Rasulullaah then stood up with him and only returned to lead the salaah after he had finished with the man."

Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi says, "Salaah would be about to commence when a person would come before Hadhrat Umar (RA) to discuss something. In fact, some of us would actually sit down because we would be standing so long." ' ' Hadhrat Moosa bin Talha says, "As he sat on the pulpit and the Mu'adhin was busy calling out the Iqaamah, I heard Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) asking people about their conditions and market prices."

The narration has already passed in the chapter discussing the straightening of rows in which Hadhrat Maalik says, "I was with Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan when the people stood up for salaah. I was busy requesting him to grant me an allowance and continued doing so as he straightened some pebbles with his shoe..."

Detailed narrations have already appeared in the chapter discussing the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and the Conquest of Madinah in which it is stated that Rasulullaah said to Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA), "O Abu Sufyaan! Accept Islaam and live in peace." After Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) accepted Islaam, he proceeded with Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) to his camp. The next morning when the Sahabah rushed to perform wudhu, Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) asked, "What is the matter with the people, O Abul Fadhl? Have they received an order?" "No," replied Hadhrat Abbaas (RA), "they are preparing for salaah." Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan then performed wudhu on the instructions of Hadhrat Abbaas who then took him to Rasululiaah. Rasulullaah ﷺ started the salaah and when he called out the Takbeer, the Sahabah (RA) followed suit. They all then made Ruku when Rasulullaah ﷺ made Ruku and got up again when Rasulullaah ﷺ got up. To this, Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) remarked, "To this day have I never seen such discipline from a nation who have been gathered together from such varying backgrounds? Neither are the nobles of Persia nor the long-established Romans as well disciplined as this!" Addressing Hadhrat Abbaas (RA), he said further, "O Abul Fadhl! Your nephew has certainly founded a great kingdom." "It is not a kingdom," Hadhrat Abbaas replied, "This is Nubuwwah."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 5 Pg.300).

paras: Another narration from Hadhrat Maymoona (RA) quoted in the chapter discussing the Conquest of Makkah states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ got up to perform wudhu, the Muslims would compete to get the wudhu water and rub it on their faces. To this, Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) remarked, "O Abul Fadhl! Your nephew has certainly founded a great kingdom." "It is not a kingdom," Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) replied, "This is Nubuwwah and it is this that the people are so zealous about."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.164) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: A narration from Hadhrat Urwa (RA) states that when Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan awoke the morning after he had spent the night with Hadhrat Abbaas he saw the Sahabah (RA) (eagerly) preparing for salaah and scattering about to purify themselves. Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) became alarmed at this sight and asked Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) what the matter was. Hadhrat Abbaas replied, "They have heard the Adhaan and are now scattering about to prepare for salaah." When salaah commenced and Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) saw the Sahabah (RA) bow and prostrate when Rasulullaah ﷺ did so, he remarked, "O Abbaas! Do they do everything he instructs them to do." "Certainly," Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) replied, "they would obey Rasulullaah ﷺ even if he were to command them to forsake their food and drink."
sources: wan Nihaayah (Vol. 4 Pg.29l).

paras: In the chapter discussing the enthusiasm Rasulullaah ﷺ had for salaah, a narration from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) has already passed stating that (when he was critically ill) Rasulullaah ﷺ sent a message to Abu Bakr to lead the salaah. Abu Bakr was a soft person so he said to Umar, "You lead the salaah, O Umar!" Umar however said, "You are more worthy of the privilege." Abu Bakr then led the salaah during those days. A narration of Bukhaari also quoted in the chapter states that Rasu'lu'llaah said, "Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in salaah," Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed. One of Rasulullaah ﷺ's wives remarked, "Abu Bakr is a soft man who will be unable lead the salaah when he stands in your place." Rasulullaah ﷺ however repeated the instruction, but again met with the same response. When this happened a third time, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "You women are just like the women around Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in salaah." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zam'ah (RA) reports, "A few Muslims and I happened to be with Rasulullaah ﷺ when his illness had become critical. When Bilaal called out the Adhaan, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Appoint someone to lead the salaah.' I left and found Umar amongst the people. Abu Bakr was not there. I therefore told Umar to lead the salaah. Umar then stood up and when he said 'Allaahu Akbar' Rasulullaah ﷺ heard his voice because his voice was very loud. Rasulullaah ﷺ then asked, 'Then where is Abu Bakr? Neither Allaah nor the Muslims can accept this! Neither Allaah nor the Muslims can accept this!' Rasulullaah ﷺ then sent for Abu Bakr and when he arrived, Umar had already completed the salaah. Abu Bakr then lead the people in salaah. Umar then said to me, 'O dear! What have you done, O Ibn Zam'ah? I swear by Allaah that when you told me to lead the salaah, I thought that it was an instruction from Rasulullaah ﷺ . Had I known better, 1 would have never led the salaah.' I explained, 'By Allaah! Rasulullaah ﷺ certainly did not instruct me to appoint you but when I did not see Abu Bakr and only saw you, 1 regarded you as being most worthy of leading the salaah.
sources: Ahmad and Abu Dawood, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol. 5 Pg.232). Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.641) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Another narration states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ heard Hadhrat Umar voice, he came out and with his head out of the room, he said angrily, "No! No! None but the son of Abu Quhaafah (i.e. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)) should lead the salaah." In the chapter discussing how the Sahabah (RA) elected Hadhrat Abu Bakr to the post of Khilaafah'3', a narration has passed in which Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah said, "I am not likely to step head of a person whom Rasulullaah ﷺ had commanded to lead us in salaah and who then led us in salaah until Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away."

Also quoted in the same chapter is the statement that Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) made when they said, "However, we are also of the opinion that Abu Bakr SSI? is most worthy of the post after Rasubllaah . He was the companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ in the cave and the 'second of the two'. We definitely acknowledge his status and his seniority. After all. Rasulullaah did instruct him to lead the Muslims in salaah while Rasulullaah ﷺ was alive."
sources: Abu Dawood, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.5 Pg.323).
Under the subheading "Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) declines to Accept the post of Khalifah and the statements of Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Zubayr iii) he is most Worthy of the Position".

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, the Ansaar said, "There should be an Ameer from us and one from you (Muhaajireen)." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then went to them and said, "Did you not know that Rasulullaah ﷺ had placed Abu Bakr forward (to lead the salaah)?" The Ansaar then said, "Allaah forbid that we should ever place ourselves ahead of Abu Bakr.
sources: Nasa'ee, as quoted in Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.206).

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ certainly instructed Abu Bakr to lead the salaah when 1 was present, neither unavailable nor ill. Therefore, to take charge of our matters of this world (as Khalifah) we are pleased to have the person whom Nabi ﷺ selected to take charge of our matters of Deen (our salaah)."
sources: Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.4 Pg.354).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Layla Kindi reports that Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) once arrived with a group of twelve or thirteen riders from amongst the companions of Rasulullaah ﷺ. When the time for salaah arrived, the others addressed Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) saying, "Go forward (to lead the salaah), O Abu Abdullaah." Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) declined saying, "We (non-Arabs) cannot lead you (Arabs) in salaah nor marry your women because it is through you that Allaah has guided us." One of the men from the group then went ahead and performed four Rakaahs salaah. After he had completed, Hadhrat Salmaan said, "Why did we need to perform four Rakaahs salaah when half of it (two Rakaahs) would have sufficed. (Since we are on a journey) We are most in need of concessions."

Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed was a slave of the Banu Usayd tribe. He prepared a meal one day and invited Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA). When the time arrived for salaah, Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) stepped forward to lead the salaah when Hadhrat Hudhayfah said to him, "Step back because the owner .of the house is entitled to leading the salaah." "Is that so, O Ibn Mas'ood?" Hadhrat Abu Dharr asked. When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) confirmed what Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, Hadhrat Abu.Dharr (RA) stepped back. Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed says, "They then put me forward (to lead the salaah) whereas I was just a slave. Nevertheless, I led them in the salaah."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 4 Pg.246).

paras: Hadhrat Naafi reports, "People had stood up for salaah in a Masjid in a district of Madinah where Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) had a property. The Imaam of the Masjid was a slave and when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) came for the salaah, the Imaam requested him to lead the salaah. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar declined saying, You have a greater right to lead the salaah in your Masjid.' The Imaam then proceeded to lead the salaah." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Handhala (RA) narrates, "We were in the house of Qais bin Sa'd bin Ubaadah with a group of Sahabah (RA) when we told him to lead the salaah. 'I cannot do so (in the presence of men better than I),' he submitted. I said, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said that a man has a greater right to the front of his bed, to the front of his animal and to lead the salaah in his house.' He then instructed one of his slaves who went forward and led the salaah."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quotftd in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.247).

paras: Hadhrat Alqama narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once visited Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) at his house. When the time for salaah arrived, Hadhrat Abu Moosa (RA) said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood "Go forward (to lead the salaah), O Abu Abdur Rahmaan because you are elder and more knowledgeable than I." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) replied, "You rather go forward because I have come your house and your Masjid. You therefore have a greater right." Hadhrat Abu Moosa (RA) then stepped forward and removed his shoes (and led the salaah). After he had completed, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) asked, "What was your reason for removing your shoes? Are you on the Waadi Muqaddas (where Hadhrat Moosa was when he had to remove his shoes)?"
sources: Bazzaar and Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.65) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA), "O Abu Moosa! You know well that the Sunnah practice is for the owner of the house to go forward (to lead the salaah)." However, Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) refused to do so until one of their slaves went forward.
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami.

paras: Hadhrat Qais bin Zuhayr (RA) says, "I once walked with Handhala bin Rabee to the Masjid of Furaat bin Hayyaan. When the time for salaah arrived, Hadhrat Furaat (RA) told Hadhrat Handhala (RA) to go forward (to lead the salaah). Hadhrat Handhala (RA) refused saying, "I cannot lead you in salaah when you are elder than me and have migrated before me. In addition to this, it is your Masjid. Hadhrat Fjoraat (RA) however said, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say something about you because of which I can never lead you in salaah." "So were you also present during the Battle of Taa'if when Rasulullaah iii sent me as a spy?" Hadhrat Handhala (RA) asked. When Hadhrat Furaat confirmed that he was present, Hadhrat Handhala (RA) stepped forward and led the salaah.

(When the salaah was over) Hadhrat Furaat (RA) (turned to the people and) said, "O tribe of Ijal! 1 have made him lead the salaah because Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent him to Taa'if as a spy and when he reported back, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, 'Your information is correct. You may return to your camp because you have been awake all night.' As he turned and left, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to us, 'Always follow him and the likes of him.
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.65). Abu Ya'la, Baghawi and Ibn Asaakir have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.28).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla (RA) narrates that when he once accompanied Hadhrat Umar (RA) to Makkah, they were received by the Hadhrat Naafi bin Alqama (RA) who was the Ameer of Makkah. "Who have you appointed as your deputy over the people?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. "Abdur Rahmaan bin Abzah came the reply. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "You chose a man from amongst the slaves over members of the Quraysh and the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ "That 1 have done," Hadhrat Naafi (RA) replied, "because I found him to be the most proficient reciter of the Qur'aan and because Makkah is a place where people from all parts gather, I wanted them to listen to Allaah's Book from a person who recited well." "Your judgement is excellent," Hadhrat Umar (RA) commended, "Abdur Rahmaan bin Abzah is certainly amongst the people whom Allaah has elevated through the Qur'aan."
sources: Abu Ya'la, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 5 Pg.216).

paras: Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) narrates that it was during the Hajj season when a large gathering of people amassed around a spring in Makkah. When the time for salaah arrived, a person who was not Arabic speaking and who belonged to the family of Hadhrat Abu Saa'ib Makhzoomi (RA) stepped forward (to lead the salaah). Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama (RA) pulled the man back and put another man forward. When the news reached Hadhrat Umar (RA), he said nothing to Hadhrat Miswar (RA) until Hadhrat Miswar (RA) arrived in Madinah. It was only when Hadhrat Miswar (RA) came to Madinah that Hadhrat Umar (RA) questioned him about it. "Give me a chance, O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" Hadhrat Miswar (RA) entreated. He then explained, "The man was not Arabic-speaking (whose recitation was unclear) and because it was during Hajj, I feared that some people who were there for Hajj would hear his recitation and adopt its non-Arabic mode of recitation." "Was that the express reason for what you did?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. When Hadhrat Miswar (RA) confirmed that it was, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, 'You did the right thing."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 4 Pg.246).

paras: Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah (RA) once led some people in salaah. When he turned to them (after completing the salaah), he said, "1 had forgotten to consult with you before going ahead and leading the salaah. Are you pleased with my salaah?" "Of course," the congregation replied, "who will be displeased with it, O selected companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Talha (RA) then s'aid, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that when a person leads others in salaah and they are displeased with him, the salaah does not even pass his ears (let alone reach the heavens)."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.68) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Umar bin Abdul Azeez once asked Hadhrat Anas (RA) why he did not perform salaah behind him(4). Hadhrat Anas (RA) replied, "I had seen Rasulullaah ﷺ perform salaah and I shall perform salaah with you only when your salaah is consistent with Rasulullaah ﷺ salaah. However, when your salaah differs from Rasulullaah ﷺ's salaah, I shall perform salaah (by myself) and then return to my family." ' Marwaan bin Hakam once asked Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) why he did not perform salaah behind him. Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) replied, "1 have seen Rasulullaah ﷺ perform salaah in a certain manner and will follow you only when your salaah conforms to his salaah. However, when your salaah differs from Rasulullaah ﷺ's salaah, I shall perform salaah (by myself) and then return to my family."
sources: Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.68).
Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.68).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Jaabir Waalidi says, "I once asked Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA)

(after he had led the salaah), 'Was the salaah of Rasulullaah ﷺ like this?' 'What did you not like about the way I performed salaah?' he asked. '(There is nothing 1 do not like but) I only wanted to know,' I replied. He said, 'Yes, it was like this, only shorter.' His Qiyaam was as long as it takes a Mu'adhin to descend from the Minaret and reach the row of salaah." Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Jaabir added, "I once saw Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) performing a very short salaah."
sources: Ahmad and Abu Ya'la, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.71).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) once said, "The salaah' we performed with Rasulullaah ﷺ was such that you people will criticise if anyone had to perform the same (because of its brevity)."
sources: Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.71).

paras: Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA) once attended a gathering and when the time for salaah arrived, the Imaam went forward and led the salaah. However, because he prolonged the sitting posture, Hadhrat Adi (RA) said after the salaah was completed, "The person leading the salaah should complete the Ruku and Sajdah properly (but not prolong the Qiyaam and sitting postures) because behind him are young children, old people, sick people, travellers and people with urgent needs." When the time arrived for the next salaah, Hadhrat Adi (RA) himself went forward and while completing the Ruku and Sajdah properly, he made the salaah brief. After completing the salaah, he turned to the people and said, "That was how we performed salaah behind Rasulullaah ﷺ. ." time expired, just as the Umayyad rulers used to do. This was why Hadhrat Anas (RA) refused to follow him in salaah. However, when Hadhrat Umar bin Abdul Azeez became the Khalifah, he stopped doing this.
sources: Tabraani and Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.73).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "After spending the night, Rasulullaah ﷺ would be summoned (to salaah) by Bilaal calling out the Adhaan. He would then get up and take a bath. 1 would then see the water dripping on his cheek and beard as he left for salaah, after which I would hear him weep in salaah."
sources: Abu Ya'la, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 2 Pg.89).

paras: Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "Tell me what the most remarkable incident that you saw with Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Aa'isha was silent for awhile and then she said, "One night Rasulullaah said to me, 'Do excuse me to worship my Rabb tonight.' 'By Allaah!' I replied, 'While I love to be near you, I also love anything that pleases you.' Rasulullaah then stood up, performed wudhu and started performing salaah. He wept so much as he was sitting that his lap became wet (with tears). He then continued weeping until his beard was drenched. He had then eventually wept so much more that the ground around him became soaked. When Bilaal came to inform him that the time for salaah had arrived, he saw Rasulullaah ﷺ weeping and asked, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ Why do you weep so much when Allaah has forgiven all your previous and future errors?' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'Should I then not be a grateful slave? A tremendous verse has been revealed to me tonight. Woe be to the person who recites it without pondering over it: (The verse is) 0 jtfi Jt Oi. 40 llii z I U Cj c Verily in the (perfect and wonderful) creation of the heavens and the earth (and whatever is within these) and in the alternation (changing) of the night and day are signs (that show's great power) for those who have intelligence (who care to ponder). (Those who have intelligence are) They who remember Allaah while standing, sitting and lying down (they do not forget Allaah at any time), and they think about the creation of the heavens and earth (so that they may be able to see Allaah s greatness in this). (Then, amazed by Allaah s creation, they say) "Our Rabb You have not created all this without a purpose! (These things certainly display Your power and greatness and have not been created in vain) We glorify Your purity (none can ever be equal to You) so save us from the punishment of the Fire (ofjahannam)..." (Surah Aal Imraan, verses ' Hadhrat Mutarraf reports from his father (RA) who says, "1 saw Rasulullaah performing salaah while there came from his chest a sound resembling the sound of a grindstone because of his weeping." '''Another narration states that the sound from Rasulullaah ﷺ's chest resembled the sound of a (boiling) pot.
sources: Abu Dawood.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Shaddaad bin Al Haad says, "I was standing in one of the last rows during the Fajr salaah and I could hear Hadhrat Umar (RA) cry aloud as he recited Surah Yusuf and reached the verse: "I complain of my sorrow and my grief only to Allaah." (Surah Yusuf, verse 86)
sources: Nasa'ee, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 3 Pg.32).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "When performing salaah behind Hadhrat Umar (RA), I could hear his weeping from three rows back."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, Sa'eed bin Mansoor, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Sa'd and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Munlakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 4 Pg.387).

paras: Hadhrat Sahl bin Sa'd (RA) says that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) could not be distracted when performing salaah.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.52).

paras: Hadhrat Mujaahid says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) would stand (still) like a stick in salaah, which was exactly as Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) used to do. That is what devotion in salaah means."
sources: Ahmad in his Zuhd, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.347).

paras: Hadhrat Mujaahid says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) would stand (still) like a stick in salaah. It is said that this was due to his devotion in salaah."
sources: Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.360).

paras: Hadhrat Ibnul Munkadir says, "Had you seen Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr performing salaah, you would surely say that he is a branch of a tree that the wind laps over. In fact, missiles fired from catapults would be falling all about (around him as he performed salaah) but he would pay no attention to them." Another narration from Hadhrat Ataa states that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr performed salaah, he was like a cane fixed in the ground. The Devotion of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) in salaah Hadhrat Zaid bin Abdullaah Shaybaani says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) walked so slowly for salaah that if an ant were walking beside him, you would say that he will not beat the ant."
Hadhrat (RA) Hibbaan says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) liked everything of his to face the Qibla when he performed salaah and would even face his thumbs towards the Qibla."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.335), as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.2 Pg.310).
IbnSa'd(Voi.4Pg.l54).

paras: Hadhrat Tawoos says, "I have never seen anyone perform salaah like Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar. He was so particular about facing the Qibla that even his face, palms and feet faced Qibla."
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg.l57).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Burdah narrates, "1 once performed salaah next to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar iS When he was in Sajdah, I heard him say, 'O Allaah!

Make Yourself the most beloved entity to me and the one I fear most.' I also heard him recite in salaah: 'O my Rabb! On account of the favours (forgiveness, know/edge and wisdom) you have given me, 1 shall never be among those who are accomplices to criminals.' (Surah Qasas, verse 17)
He also said, "Whenever I perform salaah, I hope that it will be a means of atonement (for my sins)."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.304).

paras: Hadhrat A'mash stated that whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) performed salaah, he (was so still that he) appeared to be a discarded piece of cloth.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.304).

paras: Hadhrat Ummu Roomaan (RA) says, "When Abu Bakr • once saw me leaning while performing salaah, he reprimanded me so sternly that I almost terminated my salaah. He then said, '1 heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "When any of you stand in salaah, his limbs be at ease and he should never lean to any side as the Jews do. Being at ease during salaah serves to complete the salaah.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol. 2 Pg.136) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Shaqeeq reports that he once enquired from Hadhrat Aa'isha about the optional salaahs that Rasulullaah ﷺ performed. She replied, "Rasulullaah ﷺ would perform four Rakaahs at home before the Zuhr salaah. He would then leave for the Masjid to lead the people in salaah. Thereafter, he would return to my room and perform two Rakaahs. After leading the people in Maghrib salaah, he would return to my room and perform two Rakaahs. Afterwards, he would lead the people in Isha and then return to perform two Rakaahs in my room. At night, he would perform nine Rakaahs salaah including the Witr. At times he would perform salaah for long time standing while at other times, he would perform salaah for a long time sitting. When performing salaah standing, he would perform Ruku and Sajdah from a standing position and when performing salaah sitting, he would perform Ruku and Sajdah from a sitting position. Then when dawn broke, he would perform two Rakaahs before leaving for the Masjid to lead the people ir: the Fajr salaah."
sources: Muslim, as quoted in Safwatus Safwah (Vol.1 Pg.75). Abu Dawood and Tirmidhi have also reported the narration, as quoted in Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol. 1 Pg.l 10).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah iSli.did not attach as much importance to any optional salaahs as much as he attached to the two Rakaahs of Fajr."
sources: Bukhaari, Muslim and others.

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) states, "I have not seen Rasulullaah ﷺ so eager to do any good deed as much as he was to perform the two Rakaahs before Fajr. In fact, he was not even that eager for booty."
sources: Ibn Khuzaymah, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.361).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) also mentioned that Rasulullaah ﷺ would never omit the four Rakaahs before Zuhr salaah and the two Rakaahs before Fajr. Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) reports that he once went to inform Rasulullaah ﷺ that the time for Fajr had arrived. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) occupied Hadhrat Bilaal by asking him about something until the sky had started to get very bright, Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) then started to call Rasulullaah ﷺ several times, -but Rasulullaah ﷺ did not come out. After a while, Rasulullaah ﷺ came out and after leading the salaah, Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) informed him that Hadhrat Aa'isha had occupied him by asking him about something and that (despite him calling) Rasulullaah ﷺ had delayed in coming out. Rasulullaah said, "(I was delayed because) I had been performing the two Rakaahs of Fajr." "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) asked, "(Why did you not leave it out because) The sky had already become very bright?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Even if the sky had become brighter than that, I would have still performed it and performed it well and properly."
sources: Bukhaari.

paras: Hadhrat Qaaboos reports that his father once sent someone to ask Hadhrat Aa'isha which salaah (apart from the Faraa'idh) Rasulullaah ﷺ most loved to perform with consistency. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "It was the four Rakaahs before Zuhr in which Rasulullaah ﷺ prolonged the Qiyaam and meticulously performed the Ruku and Sajdah." '"

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Saa'ib (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to perform four Rakaahs salaah after the sun had crossed the meridian but before (the Fardh of) Zuhr. To this Rasulullaah ﷺ would say, "This is the hour when the doors to the skies are opened and I would love to have my good deeds ascend through them."
sources: Ibn Maajah, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.364).

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to perform four Rakaahs before (the Fardh of) Zuhr and two Rakaahs after.
sources: Ahmad and Tirmidhi, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 1 Pg.364).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that if Rasulullaah ﷺ was unable to perform the four Rakaahs before (the Fardh of) Zuhr, he would perform them afterwards.' ' Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) says that from-the„time Rasulullaah ﷺ started staying with him, he noticed that Rasulullaah ﷺ regularly performed four Rakaahs before Zuhr and said, "The doors of the skies are opened when the sun crosses the meridian and no door closes until the Zuhr salaah has been performed. I therefore love to have a good deed of mine raised during this time.
Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Before the Asr salaah Rasulullaah ﷺ would perform four Rakaahs salaah, separating them with Salaam to the high-ranking angels and the Muslims and Mu'mineen who follow them."
sources: Tirmidhi (Pg.57).

paras: Another narration from Hadhrat Ali (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ performed two Rakaahs before Asr.
sources: Tirmidhi (Pg.57).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that after the Maghrib salaah Rasulullaah ﷺ used to perform two Rakaahs salaah in which he prolonged the recitation of the Qur'aan so long that the people in the Masjid had already dispersed (by the time he completed).
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.364) and Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.189).

paras: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said about the two Rakaahs before Fajr, "They are more beloved to me than red camels."
sources: Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.4 Pg.201),

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abdullaah reports that he once went to Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab when the latter was performing salaah before Zuhr. "What salaah is this?" Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan asked. Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "It is counted from amongst the salaah of the night (i.e. it carries the reward of the Tahajjud salaah)."
sources: Ibn Jareer.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Utba says, "I performed four Rakaahs salaah with Hadhrat Umar in his house before the Zuhr salaah."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg. 1 89).

paras: Hadhrat Hudhayfa bin Usayd reports that he noticed Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib performing four long Rakaahs of salaah after the sun has crossed its meridian and asked about it. Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ performing this salaah..." The rest of the Hadith is similar to the narration of Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) quoted above.
sources: Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.189).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Yazeed says, "Someone closest to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood informed me that after the sun had crossed its meridian, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) would stand up and perform four Rakaahs salaah in which he would recite two Surahs from the Mi'een (Surahs that have more than a hundred verses). Thereafter, when the Mu'adhin called out the Adhaan, he would dress fully and then leave (for the Masjid) for the salaah."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol. 2 Pg.221) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Aswad, Hadhrat Murra and Hadhrat Masrooq all narrate that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said, "No salaah of the day equals the salaah of the night except for the four Rakaahs before Zuhr. The virtue of this salaah over the other (optional) salaahs of the day is like the virtue of the congregational salaah over the salaah performed individually.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.221) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood is said, "No salaah of the day equals the salaah of the night except for the four Rakaahs before Zuhr because they have always been regarded as being on par with the Tahajjud salaah."
sources: Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.189).

paras: It is reported that both Hadhrat Baraa (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar performed the four Rakaahs of Sunnah salaah. ' It is also narrated that whenever the sun passes its meridian, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar would proceed to the Masjid where he would perform twelve Rakaahs salaah before the (Fardh of) Zuhr. Only then would he sit down.
sources: Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.4 Pg.fW).
Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.4 Pg.189).

paras: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) would perform eight Rakaahs salaah before the Zuhr salaah and then four Rakaahs afterwards.
sources: Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg. 1 89).

paras: and Isha Salaahs Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ emphatically advised me never to forsake three acts throughout my life. One of them is to perform four Rakaahs before Asr. I shall therefore never leave them out for as long as 1 live."
sources: Ibn Najjaar, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.191).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Faakhtah narrates that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) once mentioned that the salaahs between the Maghrib and Isha salaahs are called Salaatul Chaflah ('salaah of negligence'), he added, "Now you people have fallen into negligence (because you neglect these salaahs)."
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar is once said, "The person who performs four Rakaahs salaah after Maghrib is like the person fighting battle after battle (in the
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.4 Pg.192).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abul Qais narratesxthat Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "Never omit the Qiyaamul Layl because Rasulullaah ﷺ never left it out. Even when he was ill or very tired, he would perform it sitting down rather that leaving itout."
sources: Abu Dawoodand Ibn Khuzaymah, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.401).

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "Qiyaamul Layl became compulsory for us with the revelation of the verse: O you wrapped in a cloth! Stand up all night (in Tahajjud salaah) except for a little while (in which to take a rest)..." (Surah Muzammil, verses 1,2)

We therefore stood so long in salaah that our feet would swell. Allaah then revealed the verses granting concession when He said: Allaah knows that some of you may fall ill, others will travel in the world in search of Allaah's bounty (to earn a living) and others will fight in Allaah's path (in each of these cases, they will be unable to perform Tahajjud as they do at home). Therefore, recite (only) that of the Qur'aan (in Tahajjud) which is easy. (Although Tahajjud is not obligatory, do not neglect to) Establish (the Fardh) salaah, pay zakaah and give to Allaah a good loan (spend in charity for Allaah's pleasure). Whatever good you send ahead for yourselves (as reward to the Aakhirah), you will find it with Allaah in a better and more rewarding state. Seek forgiveness from Allaah. Verily Allaah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful. (Surah Muzammil, verse 20)
sources: Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.251) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Hishaam divorced his wife and then journeyed to Madinah to sell the property he had there. He intended to invest the money from the sale in horses and weapons to use in the Jihaad against the Romans until he died. En route, he met a group of people from his tribe who narrated to him that when six persons of his tribe also wanted to do the same thing during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ forbade them saying, "Do you not have an example in me?" Hadhrat Sa'eed then took his wife back in marriage and made the group witness to this.

He later returned to his people and informed them that he had been to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas to ask about Rasulullaah tali's Witr salaah. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Should I not tell you which person has more knowledge than anyone else about the Rasulullaah ﷺ's Witr?" When Hadhrat Sa'eed asked to know, Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) said, "Go to Aa'isha and ask her. Thereafter, 1 want you to return and inform me what she told you."

Hadhrat Sa'eed narrates further, "I then approached Hadhrat Hakeem bin Aflah to request him to accompany me to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA). He said, 'I shall not go near her because when I forbade her from speaking out against the two factions (the group of Hadhrat Ali (RA) and that of Hadhrat Mu'aawiya she still did so.' However, when I begged him in the name of Allaah, he accompanied me. When we went to her house, she recognised Hakeem and asked, 'Is that Hakeem?' When he confirmed that it was he, she asked, 'Who is that with you?' 'He is Sa'eed bin Hishaam,' Hadhrat Hakeem replied. 'Which Hishaam?' she enquired further. 'The son of Aamir,' came the reply. Hadhrat Aa'isha then made du'aa for Aamir's forgiveness and remarked, 'What an excellent man Aamir was!'

'O Ummul Mu'mineen!' I asked, 'Do tell me about Rasulullaah ﷺ's character'. 'Do you recite the Qur'aan?' Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) asked. When I confirmed that I did, she said, 'Well, the character of Rasulullaah ﷺ was the Qur'aan.' 1 then started to get up but it occurred to me to ask about Rasulullaah ﷺ's salaah at night. I therefore asked, 'O Ummul Mu'mineen! Do inform me about the salaah of Rasulullaah ﷺ (at night).' 'Do you recite the Surah of the Qur'aan (jipi C) (Surah Muzammil)?' When I told her that I did, she said, 'Allaah had made Qiyaamul Layl compulsory at the beginning of the Surah, because of which Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) stood for such long periods at night that their feet would become swollen. Allaah held the end of the Surah back in the heavens for twelve months, after which he revealed the concession. Therefore, Qiyaamul Layl became optional after it had been compulsory.'" Hadhrat Sa'eed continues, "I was again about to leave when it occurred to me to ask about the Witr salaah. Therefore, I said, 'O Ummul Mu'mineen! Do inform me about Rasulullaah ﷺ's Witr salaah. She replied, 'We would keep Rasulullaah (SSi Miswaak and wudhu water ready and when Allaah wished him to awake, he would get up, brush his teeth with the Miswaak and then perform wudhu. Rasulullaah ﷺ would then perform eight Rakaahs salaah without sitting in between (for the final sitting preceding the Salaam) except in the eighth Rakaah. He would engage in Dhikr of Allaah and making du'aa to Him while he sat, after which he got up for the ninth Rakaah without making Salaam. He would then perform the ninth Rakaah and then sit down. As he sat, he would again engage in Dhikr and du'aa before making Salaam audibly. After the Salaam, he would 186 (Vol-3) perform two Rakaahs salaah in a sitting posture. That, dear son, was eleven Rakaahs. However, as Rasulullaah ﷺ grew older and heavier, he would make the seventh Rakaah the Witr and then perform the other two Rakaahs. That, dear son, was nine Rakaahs. Whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ performed a salaah, he liked to be consistent with it and if sleep, pain or illness ever prevented him from Qiyaamul Layl, he would perform twelve Rakaahs the next day. I do not know of Rasulullaah ﷺ completing the entire Qur'aan in one night until dawn and I am also unaware of him fasting an entire month except for the month of Ramadhaan.'

I then returned to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) and when I informed him about what Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) had told me, he said, 'She is right. Had I been one to go to her, I would have reported the narration directly from her.
sources: Ahmad and Muslim, as quoted in the Tafseer of Ibn Katheer (Vol.4 Pg.435).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports, "When the beginning of Surah Muzammil was revealed, the Sahabah (RA) stood in salaah as long as they did during Ramadhaan. A year had passed between the revelation of the first part of the Surah and the last part."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Pg.281).

paras: Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) used to perform his Witr salaah at the beginning of the night and when he stood for (Tahajjud) salaah, he would perform it in units of two Rakaahs.
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.278).

paras: Hadhrat Aslam says, "Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) used to perform salaah for a long while at night and when half the night had passed, he would awaken his family for salaah, saying, 'Salaah!' He would then recite the verse: Instruct (encourage) your family to perform salaah and (you) yourself (must) remain steadfast on it. We do not ask provision (sustenance) from you, but We provide for you. The best result (reward in the for (adopting) Taqwa. (Surah, verse 132)
sources: Maalik and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.380).

paras: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that when Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abul Aas (RA) married one of Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s widows, he said, "By Allaah! I did not marry her simply for wealth or children. 1 however wanted her to inform me about Hadhrat Umar's nights (in Ibaadah)." When he asked her how it was that Hadhrat Umar would perform salaah at night, she explained, "After performing the Isha salaah, he would instruct us to place a dish of water at his headside and to keep it covered. When he then woke up at night, he would dip his hand into the water, wipe his face and hands and then engage in Dhikr for a while. (He would then doze off and) It would occur several times that he would awaken (engage in Dhikr and doze off) until the time for him to get up for the Tahajjud salaah arrived." (One of the narrators called) Ibn Buraydah asked (Hadhrat Hasan), "Who narrated this to you?" When Hadhrat Hasan replied that it was the daughter of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abul Aas (RA), Hadhrat Ibn Buraydah conformed that she was a reliable source.
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.4 Pg.380).

paras: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) loved to perform salaah in the middle of the night.
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg.289).

paras: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) used to perform salaah for a long while at night and then ask, "Naafi! Has the last portion of the night arrived?" If Hadhrat Naafi replied in the negative, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar would continue performing salaah. He would then ask later on, "Naafi! Has the last portion of the night arrived?" When Hadhrat Naafi would eventually reply that the time had arrived, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar Si! would sit down and engage in Istighfaar and du'aa until dawn broke.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.303), as quoted in lsaabah (Vol.1 Pg.349). Tabraani has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) would start performing salaah whenever he awoke during the night."

Hadhrat Abu Ghaalib says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) used to stay with us in Makkah and always performed the Tahajjud salaah. One night just before dawn he said to me, 'O Abu Ghaalib! Why don't you get up and perform salaah, even if you recite only a third of the Qur'aan?' I said, 'But how will I recite a third of the Qur'aan when dawn is so close by?' He replied, Verily Surah Ikhlaas (ji (ji-i) is equal to a third of the Qur'aan.".
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.304).

paras: Hadhrat Alqama bin Qais relates, "I once spent the night with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood. He got up during the early part of the night and started performing salaah. He recited as an Imaam in the local Masjid would recite, steadily and without adopting a singing tune. He recited audibly enough for the people around him to hear and he would not regurgitate his voice. Eventually when only that part of the night was left equal to the time it takes between the Maghrib Adhaan and the end of the Maghrib salaah, he would perform his Witr salaah."

Hadhrat Taariq bin Shihaab reports that he once spend a night with Hadhrat Salmaan to see how he exerted himself in Ibaadah at night. When Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) got up to perform salaah during the last portion of the night, Hadhrat Taariq did not get to see what he expected. When he mentioned this to Hadhrat Salmaan (RA), the Sahabi (RA) explained, "Guard your five (Fardh) salaahs closely because they for the sins you commit, except for the major sins. After people have perforrried the Isha salaah, they are divided into three groups. One of the groups has 'nothing for' them but plenty against them. The other group has something for thgrh but nothing against them, while the last group has neither anything for them nor against. The person with nothing for him but plenty against him is the one who takes advantage of the darkness of the night and obliviousness of people to outdo himself in'isinriing, because of which he has plenty of sin to his detriment and no good to his name. The person with something for him and nothing against him is the one who also takes advantage of the darkness of the night and obliviousness of people, but uses it to engage in salaah. It is for this reason that he has much to his credit but nothing to his detriment. As for the person with neither anything for him nor against, he is the one who goes to bed immediately after performing the Isha salaah. He will therefore have no sin to his account, nor any good. Beware of being hasty and always adopt moderation and constancy."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.266).

paras: Hadhrat Ummu Haani (RA) whose name was Faakhtah and who was the daughter of Abu Taalib, reports that when Makkah was conquered, she went to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. When she got to him, Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy taking a bath. After completing the bath, Rasulullaah ﷺ performed eight Rakaahs salaah, which is referred to as Salaatud Duhaa (the midmorning salaah) Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "While Rasulullaah ﷺ usually performed four Rakaahs of Salaatud Duhaa, he also sometimes increased the number of Rakaahs."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.401).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates, "I sav/ Rasulullaah ﷺ perform six Rakaahs of Salaatud Duhaa and I have never them thereafter."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol. 2 Pg.337) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Another narration from Hadhrc.t H.aani SgH2i6!sgi states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ went to her house the dty Makkah was conquered, he performed six Rakaahs Salaatud Duh?2. When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Avfa (RA) performed only two Rakaahs Salaatud Duhaa, his wife asked, "You have performed only two Rakaahs?" He replied, "Rasulullaah ﷺ also performed two F.akac, is of this salaah when he was given the good news of a victory and also when the head of Abu Jahal was brought to him."
sources: Tabraani in his Awsat and Kabeei; reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 2 Pg.238).

Bazzaar and Tabraani Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.238) has commented on the chain of narrators. Ibn Maajah has reported a similar narration, stating that Rasulullaah ﷺ performed the Salaatud Duhaa in this manner when the head of Abu Jahal was brought to him. This narration does not state that Rasulullaah ﷺ did so when receiving news of a victory.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) once said, "There is a verse of the Qur'aan that I used to recite without understanding what it referred to. The verse is: ...by evening and at Ishraaq (daybreak)... (Surah Saad, verse 18) This was until Ummu Haani narrated to me that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came to her and asked for a dish of water to make wudhu. She said, 'I could still see traces of dough in the dish (because I had just used it for making dough). Rasulullaah ﷺ however made wudhu and performed the Salaatud Duhaa saying, 'O Ummu Haanil This is the 'Ishraaq' salaah ('the daybreak salaah').
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.238) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an army, they returned very quickly with a large booty. Someone remarked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I have never before seen an army returning so quickly with such a large booty." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Shall I not inform you of an army that returns even quicker with an even larger booty? It is the person who performs wudhu properly, proceeds to the Masjid to perform the Fajr salaah and then follows this up with performing the Salaatud Duhaa. Such a person returns even quicker with an even larger booty."
sources: Abu Ya'la, Bazzaar, Ibn Hibaan and Tirmidhi, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.428). the narration of Bazzaar adds that the person referred to was Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). Ahmad and Tabraani have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.427).

paras: Hadhrat Ataa Abu Muhammad says that he saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) performing the Salaatud Duhaa in the Masjid.
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 4 Pg.281).

paras: Hadhrat Ikramah reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) would perform the Salaatud Duhaa once every ten days. The daughter of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA), Hadhrat Aa'isha narrates that (her father) Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) used to perform eight Rakaahs of Salaatud Duhaa.
sources: Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.282).
Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.283).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that although Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) did not perform the Salaatud Duhaa, he performed Nawaafil salaahs between Zuhr and Asr together with the long shift he took at night.
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.258) has commented on the chain of narrators

paras: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) engaged himself in salaah between Zuhr and Asr.
Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) says, "I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and performed the Maghrib salaah with him. Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ continued performing salaah until Isha.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.304).

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ammaar bin Yaasir reports that he saw (his father) Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) perform six Rakaahs salaah after the Maghrib salaah. Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) said, "I saw my beloved friend Rasulullaah ﷺ perform six Rakaahs salaah after the Maghrib salaah. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Whoever performs six Rakaahs salaah after the Maghrib salaah will have all his sins forgiven even though they may be as much as the foam on the oceans.
sources: Tabraani in his Thalaatha. Tabraani and Mundhiri (Vol.! Pg.368) have commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Yazeed says, "There was a time when I would always find Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) engaged in salaah. The time was between Maghrib and Isha. I once said to him, 'Whenever 1 come to you during this time, I always find you engaged in salaah (Why is this?)' He replied, 'This is a time of negligence (when people are generally negligent of Allaah).
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.230) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Aswad bin Yazeed reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "How excellent is the time of negligence i.e. the time between Maghrib and Isha."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.230) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Verily the angels surround the people who perform salaah between Maghrib and Isha, which is the Salaatul Awaabeen."
sources: Ibn Zanjway, as quoted in Kanzul Umtnaal Pg.193).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla (RA) narrates that when someone married the widow of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha (RA) and asked her about some special deed that he carried out, she replied, "He would perform two Rakaahs salaah whenever he left the house and whenever he entered."
sources: Ibn Mubaarak, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.2 Pg.306).
